headline: Amazon is reported to be moving toward buying the Israeli AI start-up Decart at a value of about $5.5 billion, below the $7 billion reported earlier.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a follow-up with a lower price and new background, from a single Israeli outlet, with nothing signed.
importance_line: Decart's staff and investors, mostly US venture funds, would get a quick sale, and Amazon's cloud customers could gain an easier way to run AI on Amazon's own chips, but the price is lower than earlier reports, nothing is signed, and Decart has not commented.
summary: CTech, the English edition of Israel's Calcalist, reports that after Anthropic dropped its plan to acquire Decart a month ago and Nvidia declined to reopen talks, Decart's shareholders turned to Amazon, and that a deal valuing the company at about $5.5 billion, below the $7 billion the Wall Street Journal reported and we carried on 12 Oct 2026, could be signed by the end of October. New today is the lower price and the account of the earlier failed talks; Decart, whose software helps AI models run efficiently on chips from different makers and which was valued at $4 billion in May, did not comment, and CTech says Amazon has long worked with the company as it develops its own Trainium chips to depend less on Nvidia.
notes: Read in full from the article body in the page data (the standard extractor found no text). Follow-up of the 12 Oct 2026 edition item 8 (WSJ report, via SiliconANGLE and CTech, of talks at about $7 billion).
